reading: Firms that will be removed from the register go dark years before the removal. For FNS-era removals the share with an original statement falls from the reference level four or five years ahead to about 20 to 30 percent one year ahead; Rosstat-era removal cohorts sat far below the reference throughout. Absence is therefore partly the leading edge of exit, not only a disclosure choice among continuing firms.
caveats: Removal is a registry event, not a verified business exit|The no-removal reference is right-censored at the 2025 release|Absence before removal is not evidence of non-submission or concealment|Horizons never cross the 2019 provider change
source_line: Foundation registry, lab aggregation; 99.97 % of eligible records have consistent identity and dates

reading: One third of the 2019 registered population reported in all six years. Two in five were absent in 2019, and two thirds of those had a recorded removal by 2024, mostly within one to three years; six percent stayed registered and absent throughout. Histories that break after years of availability (A then N or X) are individually rare but numerous in total.
caveats: FNS era only; no history crosses the provider change|A blank cell after X is expected, a blank without X is not an exit|States describe the retrieved release, not dated disclosure decisions|Firms entering after 2019 are excluded
source_line: Foundation registry 2019-2024, lab pivot of 3,413,062 firms

reading: Model-free, every supplied list shows the chapter's pattern: in the FNS era listed firms report originals far less often than other eligible firms, the government strategic list least of all. In the Rosstat archive the same groups were above other firms. The break sits exactly at the 2019 provider change, so the two eras are two collections, not one history.

reading: Among firms that reported last year, the share reporting again rises steadily with size: from about 75 percent in the smallest asset decile to about 95 percent in the largest, in both eras, with the smallest firms gaining most after 2022. Going dark is concentrated among very small firms.
